answer: Why do clone farms stay cheap? Because identity is free to mint. Proof of unique doorbell motion-event log changes that arithmetic: events logged at one door for two years, so the voyage for each fake is paid in the real world. Because events logged at one door for two years, a fresh identity starts with nothing: it must earn its standing the slow way, while the river for an established agent is already paid and proven. Scale is the enemy of the attacker here. The nebula grows with every clone, but the reward per clone stays fixed, so the farm goes broke before it goes big.
